summary: Queue heartbeat + feature-flag rollout causing soft 429s for Private deployment
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightDocs reported intermittent 429 responses for a single API key after we rolled out a priority-weighting feature flag to their private deployment. The pattern appears during concurrent webhook reconnect storms and internal queue heartbeats.

Impact:
- Customer is seeing ~10-15% of requests return 429 over a 3 minute window during their webhook reconnect/flush cycles (affects ingestion pipeline and synchronous chat endpoints).
- This is a private deployment (VPC) with on-prem Redis job queue and a custom health/heartbeat probe. Business impact: ingestion backpressure and delayed customer-facing responses.

Environment:
- Private control plane, us-west-2 region
- Dedicated private-managed ingress + local Redis queue
- Feature flag: priority-weighted-routing=v2 enabled (rolled out via console on 2026-03-11 02:20 UTC)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Enable feature flag priority-weighted-routing=v2 on the private deployment.
2) Trigger ~200 concurrent webhook reconnects (short-lived POSTs) + start background queue worker that does heartbeat pings every 2s.
3) Observe client-reported 429s on chat and ingest endpoints within ~90–180s of activity spike.

Observed behaviour:
- 429s include x-rate-limit and x-retry-after headers, but remaining/limit counters look inconsistent across edge and origin.
- Throttling appears per-API-key; other tenants on same private cluster not affected.
- No obvious GPU or serving runtime saturation.

Expected behaviour:
- Priority-weighted rollout should not cause token double-counting or count health probes as billable requests.

Relevant logs/traces (customer/edge):
- Edge proxy logs show many HEAD/OPTIONS and short POSTs during reconnect window.
- Rate-limiter trace sample: token_window refills show a ~30s misalignment between edge and origin accounting.
- Redis-side queue: heartbeats processed but also trigger a synchronous status callback that hits the API route.

Attachments:
- customer-sampled-edge-logs-2026-03-11.tar.gz (uploaded to ticket)
- heap snapshots and rate-limiter metrics dashboard links included in related_confluence_pages
investigation_notes:
Timeline and hypotheses:
- 2026-03-11 03:00 UTC: Support replicated short reconnect flood using customer's repro script against staging private cluster.
- Observed the same soft-429 pattern when heartbeat callbacks were enabled at the same time as the flag.
- Metrics: token_bucket_consume_count increments twice in many traces: once at ingress proxy, again at origin due to route rewrite. Suspect header rewrite/health-probe path causing duplicate accounting between edge and origin.
- Hypothesis A: In private deployment, the ingress proxy rewrite strips an internal header so origin treats the request as new and re-applies token accounting.
- Hypothesis B: Feature-flag v2 changes route weight which moves some requests to a canary route that has a different quota window leading to transient double-billing during window boundary.
- Observed that the customer's queue worker sends a synchronous status callback to /v1/tasks/ack (same API key) which is not excluded from quota by default and looks like user traffic. Combined with short-lived webhooks this produces token burst beyond burst-pool.
- Cross-checked with rate-limiter service logs: there is a window_refill jitter of ~2-4s caused by local clock skew on the private control plane nodes (customer's NTP drift was 1.8s on average). This exacerbates sawtooth refill behavior.

Actions taken so far:
- Added temporary debug logging at ingress and origin to correlate request ids.
- Reproduced issue in our internal private staging using customer's repro to confirm counting duplication.
- Escalated to infra (rate-limiter) and private-control-plane teams; created github PR to add an opt-out header for internal callbacks.
- Applied temporary configuration change on customer's private cluster: exclude /v1/tasks/* from quota accounting for API key scope flagged as internal-callbacks.
resolution:
Workaround applied and next steps:
- 2026-03-12 08:10 UTC: Applied immediate workaround on customer's cluster: added rule to explicitly exempt queue callback endpoints (/v1/tasks/ack, /v1/tasks/heartbeat) from rate accounting for API keys labeled internal-callback. This reduced 429s to <1% during repro window.
- 2026-03-13 14:30 UTC: Rolled back the priority-weighting=v2 rollout to previous stable variant for the customer (to remove canary route mismatch). 429 rate returned to baseline.
- Planned permanent fixes:
  1) PR (github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4872) adds an opt-out header X-Internal-Callback that short-circuits rate-accounting at the edge if present and signed by control-plane.
  2) Add a configuration knob in Private Console to map health/heartbeat paths to internal-callers exception lists.
  3) Run NTP + clock drift remediation checklist in the customer's private control plane nodes to reduce window jitter.
- Follow-up items: schedule a joint runbook session with BrightDocs engineering to update their worker to use the internal-callback header and to avoid synchronous ack callbacks when possible. Target deploy of infra fix: 2026-03-22.
